name: Bahrain (5th Fleet)
note: 5th Fleet HQ. Direct control of Gulf naval assets. Day 96 (June 3): Bahrain's army intercepted three Iranian ballistic missiles and several drones; the IRGC claimed strikes on the 5th Fleet HQ, an airbase, and helicopters, which CENTCOM denied as false. The US naval blockade of Iranian ports ended May 29 (Trump announcement) — the dual Gulf blockade is now eased on the US side, though Iran's selective Hormuz closure persists. Day 98 (June 5): Bahrain intercepted 3 Iranian ballistic missiles plus several drones in Iran's June 5 salvo (all intercepted, no casualties); CENTCOM also downed IRGC drones near Hormuz over June 5-6. Day 103 (June 10): Iran struck again in retaliation for the June 9 US strikes — the IRGC launched drones at the US Fifth Fleet HQ; Bahrain's defenses intercepted/repelled them with no US casualties or damage reported (IRGC battle-damage claims UNVERIFIED and US-disputed). Day 110 (June 17): No new strikes on US bases June 11-17; the released 14-point MOU commits the US to lift the naval blockade on the June 19 signing and to withdraw forces 'from surrounding areas' within 30 days of a final agreement, though a June 15 US advisory says the blockade remains in effect until the signing). Day 121 (June 28): TARGETED AGAIN — the IRGC fired missiles and drones at US 5th Fleet / NSA Bahrain in retaliation for the June 26-27 US strikes on Iranian territory; an 8-story residential building in Muharraq was hit and its top floor destroyed (no deaths), and Bahrain's FM called it a 'dangerous escalation.' The IRGC claimed 8 US military sites struck; a US official said no intended targets were impacted. A 'stand down for now' followed June 28-29. The US 60-day Iran oil sanctions waiver (General License X) remains valid through Aug 21. Day 137 (July 7-14): CEASEFIRE COLLAPSED — sirens sounded at NSA Bahrain/Juffair three times (Jul 8, 12, 13) as Iran resumed missile/drone waves; the IRGC claimed strikes on the 5th Fleet HQ area and Sheikh Isa AB as part of its '80+/85 US sites' response (claims UNVERIFIED); downed drones damaged Bahraini homes; NO confirmed US casualties (CENTCOM).

name: Prince Sultan AB (Saudi Arabia)
note: Key US/coalition air base in the Kingdom. Day 68-69 (May 6-7): Saudi Arabia suspended US base/airspace access for Project Freedom (NBC News May 6 / AP May 7); 43 aircraft (13 KC-135, 6 E-3G AWACS) reportedly grounded during the 4-day suspension per House of Saud / Al-Monitor satellite imagery. Day 70-71 (May 7-8): Restrictions LIFTED after a second Trump–MBS phone call (WSJ, Türkiye Today, The Defense News May 8). WSJ: Pentagon could resume Project Freedom 'as early as this week.' Anonymous Saudi source to Al-Hadath: Kingdom 'did not allow the use of its airspace to support offensive military operations' — public Saudi line at variance with WSJ characterization (PARTIAL-CONFIRM). Major precedent for real-time GCC ABO leverage. Day 137 REGIONAL (July 13): the Houthi-Saudi truce (since March 2022) BROKE — after alleged strikes on Sanaa International Airport (aimed at blocking an Iranian air bridge), Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at Saudi Arabia's Abha airport, their first attack on the kingdom in over four years, declaring the 'de-escalation phase' over; Houthis also warned airlines off Saudi airspace.

name: Ali Al Salem AB (Kuwait)
note: 386th Air Expeditionary Wing hub. Day 68-69 (May 6-7): Kuwait restricted overflight for offensive Project Freedom-related operations (NBC News May 6); Camp Arifjan houses largest US troop concentration in Middle East and ARCENT forward HQ. Day 70-71 (May 7-8): RESTRICTIONS LIFTED — Kuwaiti overflight restored after diplomatic intercession (WSJ; Drop Site News). Day 72 dawn (May 10) preview: Kuwait MoD (Brig. Gen. Saud Abdulaziz Al-Otaibi) reported armed forces 'detected and dealt with several hostile drones within Kuwaiti airspace.' Day 89-90 (May 27-28): Kuwait REACTIVATED air defenses — Kuwaiti forces INTERCEPTED an Iranian ballistic missile fired at Kuwait at 10:17 p.m. ET May 27 (CENTCOM called it an 'egregious ceasefire violation'); Kuwait's army said it was 'responding to hostile missile and drone threats' and the Foreign Ministry condemned the 'sinful Iranian attacks.' The IRGC claimed it had struck a U.S. air base in Kuwait in retaliation for U.S. strikes near Bandar Abbas. REGIONAL (May 28): Treasury Sec. Scott Bessent threatened Oman with sanctions if it facilitates Hormuz tolls. Day 95-96 (June 2-3): Iran struck Kuwait again — a June 3 drone/missile strike on Kuwait International Airport killed one Indian national and wounded 63+, briefly closing a terminal; Kuwait's Defense Ministry said it destroyed 12+ missiles and ~12 drones over June 2-3, and Kuwait expelled two Iranian diplomats. Day 98 (June 5): Kuwait intercepted 7 Iranian ballistic missiles in the June 5 salvo launched after the US coastal-radar strikes at Qeshm and Goruk (all intercepted, no casualties). Day 103 (June 10): the IRGC launched drones at Ali Al Salem Air Base in retaliation for the June 9 US strikes; all intercepted, no casualties or damage reported. Day 117 (June 24): US Embassy Kuwait REOPENED — operations resumed at midnight June 24 (Secretary of State Rubio held a flag-raising during a Gulf tour of the UAE, Kuwait and Bahrain) after the March suspension caused by Iranian drone attacks; this is a re-establishment, not a drawdown. NO US troop withdrawal has begun — per the MOU text, the US obligation to remove its forces from the proximity of Iran triggers only 'within 30 days after the final Deal,' and no final Deal yet exists (the 60-day negotiation window runs from June 17), so the withdrawal clock has not started. Carriers Lincoln and Bush remain on station in the Arabian Sea; VP Vance said IRGC and US military reps would be posted in Doha as a de-confliction channel. Day 121 (June 28): TARGETED AGAIN — the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at Ali Al Salem AB in retaliation for the June 26-27 US strikes on Iranian territory; Kuwait intercepted 2 ballistic missiles with no damage. A 'stand down for now' followed June 28-29; the withdrawal clock still has not started (no final Deal exists). Day 137 (July 7-14): CEASEFIRE COLLAPSED — IRGC-claimed strikes on Ali Al Salem AB (and Camp Arifjan) Jul 8-13; Kuwait's army engaged 'hostile aerial targets'; IRGC claimed 2 HIMARS launchers destroyed (UNVERIFIED by Kuwait/US); no confirmed damage or US casualties. Iran also struck a Kuwaiti offshore oil platform and 3 northern border posts Jul 12 (1 worker injured).

name: Azraq AB / Muwaffaq Salti (Jordan)
note: Hosts US Air Forces Central's 323rd Air Expeditionary Wing (~3,800 troops); reported to host MQ-9 Reapers and has supported F-16/F-35 operations; ~60 miles (100km) NE of Amman. Day 103 (June 10): TARGETED for the first time in the war — Iran fired long-range ballistic missiles at Azraq, the war's DEEPEST Iranian reach (~1,000km from the Iranian coast), in retaliation for the June 9 US strikes; Jordan intercepted 5 missiles (debris only, no casualties). The IRGC claimed (UNVERIFIED, US-disputed) it destroyed an F-35 hangar at Azraq. Day 137 (July 12-14): TARGETED AGAIN — Iran claimed strikes on a US command-and-control center and drone hangars in the Prince Hassan AB / Azraq area; Jordan repeatedly reported intercepting 4 missiles entering its airspace from Iran (Jul 12-14), with shrapnel falling in several areas; no casualties (Jordan Armed Forces / Petra).

name: RAF Fairford
note: UK. B-52 forward deployment for CENTCOM operations.

name: Pentagon
note: DoD HQ. Where Operation Epic Fury is commanded.

name: Houston
note: US energy capital. Refinery hub feeling Hormuz closure.

name: Camp Arifjan (Kuwait)
note: US Army Central (ARCENT) forward HQ; largest US troop concentration in the Middle East. Day 137 (July 8): NAMED A TARGET for the first time — the IRGC named Camp Arifjan (with Ali Al Salem AB) among targets of its Jul 8 missile/drone response, claiming HIMARS launchers and ammunition depots were hit; claims UNVERIFIED by Kuwait/US, no confirmed damage or US casualties (Kuwait General Staff / CENTCOM).

name: Kuwait offshore oil platform
note: Offshore oil drilling platform in Kuwaiti territorial waters. Day 137 (July 12): STRUCK by Iran — 1 worker injured, with material damage also reported at 3 northern Kuwaiti border posts (Kuwait Defense Ministry, Col. Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan). First strike on Kuwaiti offshore energy infrastructure of the war; helped drive the Jul 13 oil-price spike (Brent +9.59%).

name: Oman radar sites (Musandam / Al Wusta)
note: Long-range / vessel-detection radar sites in Oman's Musandam and Al Wusta governorates. Day 137 (July 12): IRGC-claimed drone strikes — damage claimed by the IRGC (UNVERIFIED); Oman summoned Iran's ambassador in protest (Oman Foreign Ministry).
